exposure: Two study periods: 15 months in 2012-2013 and 2017-2018
interventions to increase breast milk (BM) consumption
outcome: Availability of breast milk (BM) within 24 hours after delivery
cohort: 3,018 newborn infants hospitalized in the neonatal unit during two periods (2012-2013 and 2017-2018)
finding: Interventions supporting breast milk feeding in the neonatal unit were associated with improved initiation of breast milk expression and higher rates of breast milk feeding at discharge, while factors like cesarean delivery, very low birth weight, and longer hospital stays were associated with lower rates.
mod_finding: Cesarean section delivery was independently associated with delayed initiation of breast milk expression.
birth_weight: Infants admitted to the neonatal unit, including very low birth weight infants
